schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE `atom` (
  `atom_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `molecule_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  `element` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`atom_id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`molecule_id`) REFERENCES `molecule` (`molecule_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `bond` (
  `bond_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `molecule_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  `bond_type` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`bond_id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`molecule_id`) REFERENCES `molecule` (`molecule_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `connected` (
  `atom_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `atom_id2` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `bond_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`atom_id`,`atom_id2`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`atom_id`) REFERENCES `atom` (`atom_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (`atom_id2`) REFERENCES `atom` (`atom_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (`bond_id`) REFERENCES `bond` (`bond_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE `molecule` (
  `molecule_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `label` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`molecule_id`)
);
q1: SELECT DISTINCT T2.molecule_id FROM bond AS T1 INNER JOIN molecule AS T2 ON T1.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id WHERE T1.bond_type = '#' AND T2.label = '+'
q2: SELECT molecule_id FROM molecule WHERE label = '+' AND molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '#')
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT T2.molecule_id FROM bond AS T1 INNER JOIN molecule AS T2 ON T1.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id WHERE T1.bond_type = '#' AND T2.label = '+'
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT molecule_id FROM molecule WHERE label = '+' AND molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '#')
counterexample: INSERT INTO molecule (molecule_id, label) VALUES ('M1', '+'); INSERT INTO bond (bond_id, molecule_id, bond_type) VALUES ('B1', 'M1', '#'), ('B2', 'M1', '#');
explanation: Q1 uses DISTINCT to ensure that each molecule_id is only returned once, even if it appears multiple times in the bond table with the bond_type '#'. Q2, on the other hand, does not use DISTINCT, so it may return the same molecule_id multiple times if it appears in the bond table with the bond_type '#' more than once.
counterexample_dsp: Create a molecule with the label '+' and two bonds of type '#' with the same molecule_id. Q1 should return the molecule_id once, while Q2 may return it twice.
